summary: Contestants research, design, and create a 3D model or scene based on the topic 'Future Digital Workspace.' They submit a combined PDF with required documentation and present their model to judges, demonstrating technical and artistic skills. The event includes both a technical submission and a live presentation, with scoring based on detailed rubrics.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
submission_requirements: Submit all required items in one combined PDF
Upload completed projects to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
Contestant ID is required for all submissions
Materials must follow BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
Cite all sources, including oneself, on the Works Cited page
Secure a signed BPA Release Form(s) from any person whose image or work is used in the project
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for presentation
competencies: Create comprehensive profiles for characters, environments, or objects and demonstrate iterative development through research, concept art, digital prototyping, and refinement using collaborative platforms and version control.
Apply finishing, lighting, and texturing techniques using modern 3D software and design precise geometric models to meet technical and aesthetic requirements.

Employ artistic techniques —including digital painting, sculpting, and compositing—and conduct targeted research to inform design decisions, synthesizing findings into compelling visual presentations.

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

Contestant submitted documentation as one (1) PDF file: 1. Clickable URL to 3D Model 2. Concept Art 3. One-Page Profile 4. Works Cited (formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual) 5. BPA Release Form(s) 6. AI Usage and Documentation Form

rubric.description: Profile is detailed, creative, and thoroughly describes the model’s appearance, abilities, origins, and accessories, enhancing the model’s narrative.
Concept art is well-developed, visually appealing, and clearly illustrates the model’s design and special features, effectively bridging concept to model.
Model exhibits exceptional topology with optimized, efficient, and clean geometry, suitable for animation or game use without mesh issues.
Textures, materials, lighting, and shading are expertly applied to create a polished, realistic, and visually striking final model.
Special features and accessories are thoughtfully designed and seamlessly integrated, adding depth and storytelling value to the model.
Consistent, skillful use of multiple advanced techniques, greatly enhancing the realism, intricacy, and visual impact of the final product.
Model is highly original, imaginative, and creatively interprets the profile and prompt, standing out as an engaging, one-of-a-kind creation.
Model is visually striking, highly creative, and fully realizes the model described in the profile while exceeding prompt expectations.
Model exhibits exceptional topology with optimized, efficient, and clean geometry, suitable for animation or game use without mesh issues.
The text is clean, polished, and free of grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors.

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines, and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Contestant maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
The presentation content flows adequately, and the contestant demonstrates a clear and well-integrated structure throughout.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.

judging_notes: Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant and within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Finals may be part of the competition
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
eligibility_notes: Any secondary division contestant may enter this judged event
Contestants must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
